text.en: Dry ash, applied after the sandal paste.
If any of the offerings is not available, you can use akṣatas instead.

Throughout the rite the right hand acts towards the deity and the left anchors you: the right offers, holds the spoon and pours. The left rings the bell or rests on your own heart, and it pours only once — into your own right palm at ācamanam, which is purification and not an offering.
What is offered is measured against your means, not against the size of the image. A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — given with devotion, that is the offering.

Deva may be substituted by any other deity, such as Mahāgaṇapati, Mahāviṣṇu, Mahāsarasvatī or Mahālakṣmī. Choose the deity once, in the reader settings, and it is named throughout — in the saṅkalpa and in the mantras of invocation.

text.en: bathe, put on freshly washed clothes, and make the altar ready
Take a bath.
Wear clothes that have just been washed.
Tie your hair.
Keep pets out of the room.
Clean the altar and remove the previous day's offerings.
Wash the vessels and the items you will use.
Do not eat beforehand — preferably nothing at all. No non-vegetarian food: no meat, fish or eggs, and no onion or garlic.

text.en: set everything within reach before you sit down
An altar, with a vigraha — an image of the deity — or a picture of the deity.
An oil lamp, with oil and a wick: sesame oil or ghee.
Akṣatas — unbroken rice grains, with turmeric powder added.
A pañcapātra: a vessel of water with a spoon, for offering water.
Candana, sandal paste; and kuṅkuma, vermilion.
Dhūpa — incense sticks; and dīpa — a small oil lamp.
Naivedya, the food to be offered; and puṣpa, flowers, kept on a plate.
A ghaṇṭā, the bell; and karpūra, camphor, with a holder to burn it in.
If any one of the offerings is not available, you may use akṣatas in its place. This holds throughout the rite.

text.en: The right hand takes the shape called gokarṇa, the cow's ear, and the books do not agree on it. One description bends the tip of the thumb to the middle joint of the middle finger; another spreads the thumb and the little finger apart and holds the three middle fingers together and upright.
